critic_feedback: There are no previous true-fitness measurements, so recommendations must rely on the structured mutation-level feedback and the supplied model scores. The feedback is internally contradictory at the position level: nearly every mutable position is listed as both successful and failed, and the candidate annotations consequently report both supported and failed positions. I therefore treated explicit successful_mutations as the more informative signal, while avoiding substitutions absent from that list. The selected candidates are compact three-mutation designs and avoid the available four-mutation backgrounds, reducing confounding and risk while still sampling high predicted-fitness combinations.

critic_feedback: The previous round showed that the strongest signal came from combinations involving positions 578, 579, and 587, especially S578D or S578E together with V579A and N587M or N587T. However, the same positions and some mutations also appeared in low-fitness variants, demonstrating strong context dependence rather than universally beneficial effects. The new recommendations therefore prioritize available candidates retaining S578D/S578E, V579A, or N587T, while avoiding explicitly failed positions 575, 581, and 582 and generally avoiding R588A. A smaller exploratory set with high model predictions and no known failed-position overlap is included to reduce overcommitment to the confounded 578/579/587 motif.

Consequently, the recommendations are driven by motif-level evidence and cautious diversification rather than reliable single-mutation effect estimates.

critic_feedback: The previous round identified a strong positive core consisting of S578E, V579A, S580A, R566S, R585H, and especially N587G in the top candidate. However, several substitutions that looked attractive by position-level scoring—particularly R585V, N587T, R588N, S578D, and R566V—were associated with low fitness. V579A is context-dependent: it contributed to the best construct but also appeared in weaker constructs, so it should be selected only with stronger partner mutations. This round therefore prioritizes candidates carrying exact validated substitutions, especially S580A/R585H, R566S, and S578E, while favoring compact or low-risk backgrounds. Candidates dominated by the failed substitutions or by heavily negative feedback were excluded even when their predicted fitness was high.

Compare V579A-containing constructs against candidates lacking V579A to resolve its context dependence. Use results to distinguish genuinely beneficial mutation combinations from apparent position-level associations and to identify whether novel substitutions such as T581D, T581S, Q575C, or Q575T are compatible with the validated core.
